title: At least one of the 2-adic zeta values ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9) is irrational
summary: A Lean 4 and Mathlib proof that at least one of the 2-adic zeta values ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9) is irrational. The theorem has no hypotheses, and its proof uses only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The values are defined through the Volkenborn integral: zeta2 s = J(s−1)/((s−1)·2^s), where J(s) is the 2-adic limit of the Riemann sums 2^(−N) Σ_{x<2^N} (x+1/2)^(−s), and the theorem also proves that these limits exist. By Lemma 2.8 of Lai, Sprang and Zudilin (IMRN 2026), zeta2 s is the Kubota–Leopoldt value ζ₂(s) = L₂(s, ω^(1−s)) for s ≥ 2. That identification is cited, not formalised;…

review.reason: Lean 4 proof that one of two 2-adic zeta values is irrational.
